note: The configure/meson flag sets the two forks actually pass, as DATA. This is not a build system and it
does not generate anything: it is the list a bump is audited against, and the list the cross-platform
`shared` is the exact intersection of the two platforms' AUDIO flag sets. `android` and `darwin` hold
the remainder, and every flag in them MUST be covered by a `divergences` bucket: `workshop verify` fails
on an undeclared platform-only flag and on a declared flag that is no longer platform-only.
The divergence check runs on the AUDIO variant only. Android builds no video variant at all, so every
darwin video flag would otherwise be reported as divergence; that scope is recorded here for the
option-semantics audit and for the day video ships, not for the parity gate.
CAVEAT, stated once and meant: these are DECLARED flags, not shipped artifacts. FFmpeg auto-selects
components through _select/_deps chains, so a flag being absent here does not prove a component is
absent from the binary. The findings below are strong signals and concrete parity work; confirming any
of them needs a shipped-artifact probe, which is the next phase of this repo.

lgpl.statement: Every artifact rn-media ships is LGPLv3. No GPL code, no nonfree code, no exceptions.
notes: FFmpeg gates GPL-only components with <name>_deps="gpl", and in the 8.1 line every one of those
entries is a VIDEO filter (eq, hqdn3d, delogo, spp, pp, pullup, ...). No audio filter we enable
carries a gpl dep — which is the whole reason the filter allow-list is as long as it is and no longer.
mpv has no --enable-lgpl. GPL is a PERMISSION flag there: GPL-only components gate themselves with
.require(get_option('gpl')) and, being value:'auto', silently disable. Same licence outcome,
opposite polarity — which is exactly why -Dgpl=false must be asserted rather than assumed.
LIVE HAZARD: the darwin fork carries an `encodersgpl` flavour whose video_encodersgpl_options passes
--enable-gpl and links libx264. Nothing asserts that the shipped dylib was not built from it; the
only guard today is the Makefile default target string. See divergence ffmpeg-lgpl-polarity.

source.darwin: libmpv-darwin-build nix/packages/mk-pkg-ffmpeg/meson.build (disable_all_options + common_options + audio_common_options + audio_default_options; video_* for the video scope)

divergences.reason: Same intent, two spellings. Darwin reaches "the allow-list is the whole world" with --disable-all --disable-autodetect; Android enumerates the component classes and the autodetected libraries one by one. Identical outcome, and the enumerated form is arguably better documentation — but it is also why a naive diff of the two configure lines is useless, which is what this manifest exists to fix.

--enable-jni is what makes libavcodec able to reach the JVM, and is the whole reason patch 001 exists. --disable-mediacodec keeps the hardware VIDEO decoder out of an audio engine; --disable-videotoolbox is the Apple counterpart Android must not have. None of these has a meaningful darwin equivalent.
AudioToolbox is the Apple resampler/codec path and has no Android counterpart; Android disables it explicitly and darwin enables it. This is the platform ceiling being platform-shaped, not drift.

The two forks link FFmpeg differently and always have: Android builds static FFmpeg archives and links them into one libmpv.so (hence --enable-static plus the version script), darwin ships FFmpeg as separate dylibs inside the xcframework (hence --enable-shared --enable-pic). Everything here follows from that one decision. --disable-x86asm is arm-only cross-compilation; the stripping/optimization/pthreads pairs are darwin re-enabling in common_options what disable_all_options turned off.

Android ships four ABIs including armeabi-v7a, where the NEON/VFP baseline genuinely varies between devices, so runtime detection earns its size. Every Apple target we ship is arm64 with a fixed feature baseline, so darwin turns it off and takes the smaller binary.

Android's audio build passes --disable-hwaccels; darwin's audio build passes no hwaccel flag at all and darwin's VIDEO variant enumerates seven specific --enable-hwaccel=*_videotoolbox entries. This is not a capability difference between the two AUDIO artifacts: Android's flag used to be the blanket --enable-hwaccels, which resolved to nothing, because every hwaccel in FFmpeg 8.1.2 needs one of dxva2/vaapi/vdpau/videotoolbox/mediacodec/vulkan/d3d11va/nvdec and the Android configure disables all of them — `CONFIG_*_HWACCEL 1` appears exactly 0 times in the built tree. Changed to the negative in rn-media #30 so the recorded configure line stops advertising a capability the build cannot have. Darwin needs no equivalent: it never passed the blanket flag.

resolved.how: Removed from Android. This is an audio engine and nothing in rn-media encodes an image; the five encoders were inherited from the upstream flavour script and darwin never had them. The DECODERS are the cover-art feature and darwin gained those in the same release.

Removed from Android, along with the libxml2 dependency itself. FFmpeg uses libxml2 only for the DASH demuxer and neither fork enables that demuxer, so Android was linking an XML parser nothing could reach. Both audio artifacts now have neither. If DASH is ever wanted, both platforms get it together.

darwin audio_default_options gained bmp gif jpeg2000 jpegls mjpeg png tiff webp. EIGHT, not the nine Android had: --enable-decoder=ljpeg matches nothing in any FFmpeg (ljpeg is an encoder only) and was deleted from Android rather than copied here.
darwin gained --enable-decoder=truehd and --enable-demuxer=dtshd; it already had the truehd demuxer and the dca decoder, so a .thd demuxed and then failed to decode.

Android gained --enable-zlib (Matroska compressed track headers). CORRECTED 2026-08-12 (rn-media #30): this said it "adds one DT_NEEDED" and that is wrong about the shipped artifact. The NDK sysroot ships a STATIC libz.a next to libz.so, mpv.sh passes -Dprefer_static=true, so meson resolves -lz to the archive and zlib is linked INTO libmpv.so. Measured on the release .so: DT_NEEDED is exactly libm/libandroid/libdl/libc with no libz, and `nm` finds inflate/inflateInit2_ as local text. Still free in the sense that mattered (no vendored source, no new file to ship); it is ~90 KB of .text rather than a shared-library reference.

darwin common_options now ASSERTS --disable-gpl --disable-nonfree instead of leaving them commented out. Both forks now state the licence rather than one stating it and the other omitting the opposite.

Deleted on BOTH forks rather than propagated: --enable-decoder=ljpeg and --enable-protocol=srt (Android), --enable-protocol=hls (both). All three matched nothing in FFmpeg 8.1.2 and configure warned about them on every build.

BOTH forks drop --enable-filter=overlay from the AUDIO flag set. overlay is a video filter: it composites one video frame onto another, and it predates every audio filter in this list — it is one of the two entries the upstream flavour script shipped, so it was inherited, never chosen. Neither audio engine can reach it (vid=no, vo=null; mpv touches libavfilter only through filters/f_lavfi.c and the audio graph rejects a video filter at format negotiation). Measured on Android arm64 by linker --why-extract, not estimate: allfilters.o pulls vf_overlay.o (50,080 allocated bytes), which alone pulls framesync.o (3,956) and drawutils.o (6,956); the shipped .so shrank 69,016 bytes. It is listed here rather than per-fork BECAUSE it is a parity change — dropping it on one fork only would re-diverge the two audio artifacts. All 17 audio filters are untouched and asserted present on both shipped artifacts.

Android's --enable-hwaccels becomes --disable-hwaccels. Worth ZERO bytes, which is the point: every hwaccel in FFmpeg 8.1.2 requires one of dxva2/vaapi/vdpau/videotoolbox/mediacodec/vulkan/d3d11va/nvdec, and the Android configure disables all of them, so the built tree contains `CONFIG_*_HWACCEL 1` exactly 0 times (counted in _build-arm64/config_components.h). Same class of dead flag as the three the parity release deleted — asking for something the build cannot have, while reading like a capability in the recorded configure line. NO darwin counterpart is needed and none is added: darwin's audio variant never passed the blanket flag, and its video variant enumerates seven specific --enable-hwaccel=*_videotoolbox entries that do resolve. Declared as ffmpeg-hwaccels-shape.

divergences.reason: The one AO each platform actually has, and the ONLY thing left that differs between the two mpv option sets -- 103 options each, 101 identical. Android builds audiotrack and disables audiounit; iOS does the reverse. This is the platform being genuinely platform-shaped, and it is the whole of the remaining mpv divergence.

resolved.how: Aligned UP, not down. Android now VENDORS GNU libiconv 1.19 statically (buildscripts/scripts/libiconv.sh) so it can pass -Diconv=enabled at API 21, where bionic has no iconv until API 28. The first attempt aligned these by disabling iconv on darwin, which made the platforms match by removing a working feature -- the wrong direction, and the exact platform-capped compromise owning these forks is meant to prevent. Both now convert non-UTF-8 metadata, ICY stream titles, CUE sheets and playlists.

Android now passes the same exhaustive option list darwin does -- 103 options each, up from 27 -- so no mpv feature can enter either build by defaulting to `auto`. This is the avfoundation class of hazard closed on both sides. The only two options that now differ are the platform audio output (audiotrack vs audiounit).

Aligned DOWN: darwin now passes -Diconv=disabled, matching Android. Android builds at API 21 and bionic only gained iconv(3) at API 28, so enabling it there would need minSdk 28 (dropping Android 5-8) or vendoring GNU libiconv. With uchardet disabled and --metadata-codepage unset on both forks, mp_iconv_to_utf8() returns its buffer untouched anyway, so this was inert on iOS. THE LOSS: neither platform can now apply an explicit --metadata-codepage. Restoring it on BOTH is tracked in rn-media task #32.

notes: The darwin scope is the iOS effective set: DISABLE_ALL_OPTIONS then COMMON_OPTIONS then IOS_OPTIONS,
with later values winning, which is what meson sees. The macOS-only additions (-Dcoreaudio=enabled,
-Dcocoa=enabled) are not part of what rn-media ships and are deliberately not recorded here.
Export control is NOT in this list because the two forks do it with different mechanisms: Android
darwin does it with a PATCH (005-mpv-export-list) that edits library('mpv')'s own link_args. Both
lists live in assets/export-lists/ so the 55-vs-54 delta is visible in one place.
